text: The break-glass grant is created through POST /admin/break-glass-grants on P4 rwb-access and read through GET /admin/access-log on P4 rwb-access and GET /decision-log on P7 rwb-decision; POST /admin/break-glass is the legacy name of the same operation and appears in the pack only as a legacy marker.
why: The legacy story names POST /admin/break-glass and three monolith paths; the Ownership Map names the grant and access-log operations on P4 and the log query on P7.
read: RWB-E1-039 section 12; Ownership Map api rows POST /admin/break-glass-grants, GET /admin/access-log and GET /decision-log; Arch v5 slide 14.
confirm: P4 access owner and P7 decision owner
impact: The pack calls the published operations only; the parameter values, the messages and the four-hour window are unchanged.

text: A read or export fails closed only when its own local decision record cannot be written in the same transaction (DP-03); a lag of the central ledger behind rwb.decision-record.v1 is reported against the five-minute completeness target and never blocks the read, so AC7 is proved by failing the local record write in the owning service.
why: Legacy AC7 stops the decision log store; Arch v5 slide 28 separates the local record from the central ledger and keeps five-minute completeness, so the fail-closed point has to be named.
read: Arch v5 slides 20 and 28; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-03; RWB-E1-039 section 7 AC7.
confirm: P7 decision owner and Risk and Internal Audit
impact: The read still returns nothing when the record cannot be written; the central ledger stays eventually complete within five minutes.

text: The four break-glass values stay data rows read through the parameters contract of P3 rwb-case (DP-06) under the legacy names rwb.access.breakglass.window-hours, rwb.access.breakglass.incident-pattern, rwb.access.breakglass.reason-min and rwb.access.breakglass.review-days.
why: Template and Rules v1 section R3 sends parameters to P3 rwb-case and DP-06 replaces the local parameter copy; the legacy preconditions name the four parameter names.
read: RWB-E1-039 section 3; Template and Rules v1 sections R3 and R5.5 DP-06; Ownership Map tables parameter_catalog and parameter_value owner P3.
confirm: P3 case owner and P4 access owner
impact: The values stay configuration; only the owner of the parameter rows changes.

text: The reference-load path belongs to P3 rwb-case and P6 rwb-comms registers the template and merge field handlers behind the P3 published interface; the legacy P4 owner of the load endpoint is a monolith marker only.
why: The legacy story says P4 owns the load endpoint; the Ownership Map names P3 for the reference-load operations and P6 for the template and merge field tables.
read: RWB-E1-046 section 12; Ownership Map api rows POST /admin/reference-loads, POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify, POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback owner P3 and tables template and merge_field owner P6; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-07.
confirm: P3 case owner and P6 comms owner
impact: The pack loads through one published path; the refusal rules and the messages are unchanged.

text: A merge field row is checked against the P1 rwb-source-data data dictionary contract (GET /admin/data-dictionary/fields) in the same load, once per load, and a row that names an unknown field ID still refuses the whole load with MSG-P1-002.
why: The legacy story reads sys_fields through the P4 reference data interface; the Ownership Map puts sys_fields and the data dictionary operation on P1.
read: RWB-E1-046 sections 4, 7 AC4 and 11; Ownership Map tables sys_fields and sys_field_version owner P1 and api row GET /admin/data-dictionary/fields owner P1; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-11.
confirm: P1 source data owner and P6 comms owner
impact: A field ID outside the dictionary is refused in full exactly as before; the check reads one published contract.

text: The template body stays in Blob through P5 rwb-document and body_ref names it; the pack generates one letter through POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents on P5 so the P6 TemplateCatalog is read at generation time with one hop and a two-second timeout.
why: The legacy story keeps the body reference on the template and generates through the letter engine; the target splits the catalog in P6 from the document body and the generated document in P5.
read: RWB-E1-046 sections 11 and 12; Ownership Map api rows POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents and GET /documents/{documentId} owner P5, table document owner P5; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-11.
confirm: P5 document owner and P6 comms owner
impact: The current-version rule is proved at the point where a letter is generated; no template body is copied into P6.

text: The approval of a template version is written as one decision record by P6 rwb-comms in its own schema and reaches the P7 central ledger through rwb.decision-record.v1 (DP-03) with the approver, the template code and the version; no approval row is written in another service.
why: The legacy story records the Legal approval on the version but names no decision record; the target records every decision through DP-03.
read: RWB-E1-046 sections 3, 8 rule BR1 and 11; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-03; Arch v5 slides 20 and 28.
confirm: P6 comms owner and P7 decision owner
impact: The approval is traceable in one log; the load rules and the version numbering are unchanged.

text: The flag tables and the four flag operations belong to the platform library (PLT) and every service reads its values through GET /feature-flags; rwb-integration is not the owner of the flag tables in the target even though the legacy story names module P2 Integration.
why: The Ownership Map puts feature_flag and feature_flag_change with the platform library and names the four operations as PLT operations, while the legacy story names module P2.
read: RWB-E1-047 sections 3 and 12; Ownership Map tables feature_flag and feature_flag_change owner PLT and the four flag operations owner PLT; Template and Rules v1 section R3 default ruling.
impact: The pack reads and changes flags through one owner; the values, the messages and the removal date rule are unchanged.

text: The weekly removal report runs as a Temporal Schedule in the platform library at Monday 08:00 Asia/Bangkok; the Quartz trigger is retired under DP-10 while the message MSG-P2-003, the owner list and the one-report-per-date rule stay the same.
why: The legacy trigger is Quartz and Arch v5 slide 44 retires the shared Quartz tables in favour of Schedules in the owning service.
read: RWB-E1-047 sections 4 and 12; Arch v5 slide 44; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-10.
impact: The report content and its timing are unchanged; only the scheduler changes.

text: The four flag keys used as scenario data keep the legacy values rwb.casewf.case-list-queue-column, rwb.p5.ocr-intake, rwb.p6.line-dispatch and rwb.p9.unknown, because they are data rows fixed by the legacy test cases; a flag created for a wave-1 service follows the service short name under DP-14 and the two legacy prefixes stay legacy markers only.
why: DP-14 renames topics and event names, not rows already loaded, and the legacy test cases fix the four keys and their removal dates.
read: RWB-E1-047 sections 3 and 7; Arch v5 slides 42 and 43; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-14.
confirm: Platform lead and reference data owner
impact: The scenario data matches the legacy test cases; no flag row is renamed by this story.

text: The OCR step runs inside the P5 rwb-document DocumentIntakeWorkflow, started by the DocumentStored event and by the JOB-12 trigger, and a duplicate DocumentStored event creates no second intake item because the inbox dedupes it.
why: The legacy job starts the step itself after the intake and scan steps; the target starts the same step from an event and dedupes through the inbox of the consuming service.
read: RWB-E1-049 sections 3, 4 and 12; Arch v5 slide 16 (DocumentIntakeWorkflow: OCR, classify, extract), slide 42 row 16 (DocumentStored), slide 44 (JOB-12 event plus KEDA workers); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-09.
impact: One intake item per stored file; the 180-sample and 500-page runs are unchanged.

text: OCR_MIN_QUALITY, OCR_WORKERS, OCR_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and OCR_MAX_ATTEMPTS stay rows in rwb_document.document_hub_parameter under the Ownership Map, and OCR_WORKERS is read as the worker concurrency cap while the platform scales the worker count on queue depth; only business parameters go through the P3 rwb-case parameters contract.
why: DP-06 sends parameters to P3, but document_hub_parameter is a document hub table with P5 as its owner, so the four OCR values have two possible homes and the target reading has to be named.
read: RWB-E1-049 sections 3 and 13; Ownership Map table document_hub_parameter owner P5 and tables parameter_catalog and parameter_value owner P3; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-06.
confirm: P5 document owner and P3 case owner
impact: The threshold, the timeout and the attempt limit stay configuration; the worker cap keeps the 60-minute target measurable.

text: The OCR service stays an outside system called under the identity SY-OCR through the OcrClient adapter; the SIT stub is replaced by the real service for the 180-sample and 500-page runs only, and the engine version that answered is recorded on each intake item.
why: The legacy story names the OCR service, the SY-OCR identity and the stub replacement rule; the microservice target keeps the same outside system behind the same adapter.
confirm: P5 document owner and the OCR service owner
impact: The pack proves the throughput against the real service and records which engine version answered; no production call is made.

text: The classify step runs inside the P5 rwb-document DocumentIntakeWorkflow and calls the classifier as a child run of P10 rwb-agent on task queue rwb-agent (AgentRunWorkflow, 60 seconds then rule result); P5 records the returned scores and the model version on the intake item.
why: The legacy story calls the classifier through the P10 model gateway from the document job; the target gives the model call its own workflow on the agent queue.
read: RWB-E1-050 sections 3, 4 and 12; Arch v5 slide 16 (P10 IN AgentRunWorkflow 60 s then rule result; P5 IN AgentRunCompleted for classification); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-11.
confirm: P5 document owner and P10 agent owner
impact: The classifier stays behind one route; the 60-second timeout and the fallback rule are unchanged.

text: CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD, CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES and CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS stay rows in rwb_document.document_hub_parameter under the Ownership Map; only business parameters go through the P3 rwb-case parameters contract.
why: DP-06 sends parameters to P3, but document_hub_parameter is a document hub table with P5 as its owner, so the three classify values have two possible homes and the target reading has to be named.
read: RWB-E1-050 sections 3, 4 and 13; Ownership Map table document_hub_parameter owner P5 and tables parameter_catalog and parameter_value owner P3; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-06.
confirm: P5 document owner and P3 case owner
impact: The threshold, the pages read and the timeout stay configuration; a change needs no deployment.

text: The labelled sample stays 180 synthetic documents, 30 per type; the evaluation report is written to the standard container and to the job record, and the model version of each run is recorded on the intake item in classifier_version.
why: The legacy story fixes the sample size, the accuracy target and the report content but names no storage location for the report in the target.
read: RWB-E1-050 sections 3, 4, 7 AC1 and 13; Arch v5 slide 16 (P5 Blob with WORM).
confirm: P5 document owner and the risk and model risk officer
impact: The evaluation evidence is reproducible from the run record and the container; no synthetic document leaves the bank.
